mechanism_narrative: A continued recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT from their recent lows indicates more commuting and downtown foot traffic, which should lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as routine trips spill into shopping and dining visits.
evidence_refs: fact:both commuting proxies are less negative than at t-3w but still below baseline
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve over the next month but RETAIL_REC does not rise relative to the prior 28 days, the commuting-spillover mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL remains above baseline while TRANSIT stays deeply negative, discretionary shopping shifts to neighborhood and online substitution patterns that suppress destination retail visits, so RETAIL_REC falls over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -25 and RESIDENTIAL stays above +5
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is positive in all four weeks while TRANSIT is persistently around -30
failure_condition: If TRANSIT remains below -25 and RESIDENTIAL stays above +5 yet RETAIL_REC does not decline within two weeks, the substitution mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: A further easing in mobility restrictions is signaled when WORKPLACES moves closer to zero and TRANSIT rises toward its pre-period baseline; that policy-easing regime should increase RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks through more in-person activity.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -15 or TRANSIT rises above -25
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improved from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES or TRANSIT crosses the specified threshold but RETAIL_REC is not higher over the next 28 days than over the previous 28 days, the policy-easing link is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS mobility above its recent depressed level indicates better weather and outdoor recreation demand, which usually spills into nearby food, leisure, and shopping trips, pushing RETAIL_REC up within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 5 points from the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell to -23.0 at t-1w and then recovered to -15.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: If PARKS rises by at least 5 points week-on-week and RETAIL_REC does not improve within the following week, the outdoor-spillover hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A synchronized improvement in GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES signals broader normalization of routine trips and errands, which should translate into more incidental retail visits and raise RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both series are less negative at t-0w than at t-3w despite a mid-period dip
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES improve together but RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over the next month, the routine-trip carryover mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT fails to recover and stays near its current depressed level, leisure shopping remains effortful and trip chaining weakens, so RETAIL_REC stays below its previous four-week mean over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stays below -28 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is still around -29 in the latest week after several weeks below -30
failure_condition: If TRANSIT remains below -28 for two consecutive weeks but RETAIL_REC rises relative to the prior 28 days, the low-transit deterrence mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: A renewed tightening regime shows up first as weaker TRANSIT and WORKPLACES readings; under that condition, discretionary retail visits contract further over the next four weeks because commuting and office-linked shopping trips are cut back.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -32 and WORKPLACES falls below -22
evidence_refs: fact:both series were more negative at t-3w than at t-0w, suggesting a prior tightening shock
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES drop below the stated levels but RETAIL_REC does not decline over the following month, the tightening-channel hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS and RESIDENTIAL both rise together, households are substituting toward local outdoor and home-based activities, which reduces destination shopping demand and keeps RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed positive while PARKS rebounded sharply at t-0w after a weak t-1w
failure_condition: If PARKS and RESIDENTIAL both increase but RETAIL_REC does not fall relative to the last 28 days, the local-substitution mechanism fails.
